name: Ortoq — equity regime (capital entrusted)
key_source: Enkhbold 2019 (Central Asian Survey 38:4, 10.1080/02634937.2019.1652799), 542-543, from Juvayni, Rashid al-Din and Vassaf. SPLIT from the generic 'ortoq' row: the type spans both values of AP3, CF2, LR1 and LR6, which one row cannot hold. The principal bears losses capped at his investment and the agent bears none — the qirad/commenda configuration.

name: Ortoq — loan regime (capital advanced at interest)
key_source: Enkhbold 2019, 543-544, on Allsen 1989 and Otagi 1973. The second half of the split. Ortoqs 'completely liable for the loans they took, which extended beyond partnership capital to their private properties'; guarantors unconditionally bound; on default, seizure and then enslavement of the defaulter and his family (Rashid al-Din 1998, 726). The isqa configuration. Enkhbold dates and explains the shift: the Yuan government spent 76,000 ding of silver in 1240 bailing out ortoqs, and 'the huge losses suffered by Mongol elites motivated Mongol authorities to shift towards a risk-transfer model'.
